story: An artwork by Banksy shredded itself after selling for $1.3M at Sotheby’s
text: I think this one is quite interesting: [VIDEO] A motor connected to a series of reduction gears, with the last part of the chain encased in concrete.

I think the artist put it as "and then the last gear turns so slowly it doesn't really matter, so I cast it in concrete." Assuming we're talking about Arthur Gansons "Machine with concrete"[0] of course. I quite like how a lot of his work seems to have a punchline to it. [0] [VIDEO]
There is one by Arthur Ganson in the MIT museum[1]. It's part of a great exhibit of fun/quirky machines and there's an interesting video about it on youtube[2]. [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]

This reminds me of "Machine with Concrete", by Arthur Ganson: [VIDEO] From the video description: Each worm/worm gear pair reduces the speed of the motor by 1/50th. Since there are 12 pairs of gears, the final speed reduction is calculated by (1/50)12. The implications are quite large. With the motor turning around 200 revolutions per minute, it will take well over two trillion years before the final gear makes but one turn. Given the truth of this situation, it is possible to do anything at all with the final gear, even embed it in concrete.

Arthur Ganson's "Machine with Concrete" is an installation that has 1:50 gears put in sequence, to the power of 12; the last section is embedded in concrete: [VIDEO] There's also the pitch drop experiment, which IMO rivals watching grass grow: [LINK]
